items.followUp: State four differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus, whereas eukaryotic cells have one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prokaryotes lack a true nucleus or have a nucleoid, while eukaryotes have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast between prokaryotic and eukaryotic organelles.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and eukaryotic cells are generally larger.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular, while eukaryotic nuclear DNA is arranged in linear chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast in DNA form or chromosome organisation.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; their DNA lies in a nucleoid, whereas eukaryotic cells have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles, whereas eukaryotic cells contain them, such as mitochondria.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and simpler; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and more complex.
Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular and not organised into a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic nuclear DNA is arranged in linear chromosomes.
